To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

chronic intermittent ethanol (a rat model of alcohol dependence) causes significant long-lasting alterations in membrane properties, K+ currents, and glutamateric synaptic transmission of NAcc medium spiny neurons, which could play an important role in the neuroadaptations that underlie alcohol withdrawal and dependence.
the intrinsic membrane properties and excitatory synaptic transmission of NAcc MSNs are significantly altered by CIE treatment and protracted withdrawal.

chronic intermittent exposure to ethanol causes long-lasting alterations in the membrane properties of medium spiny GABAergic neurons in the nucleus accumbens, including increases in K+-currents and in the conductance and amplitude of α-amino 3-hydroxy 5-methyl 4-isoxazole propionic acid receptor-mediated synaptic currents, which could contribute to the neuroplastic changes underlying alcohol withdrawal.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of chronic alcohol exposure on the electrophysiological properties of neurons of the nucleus accumbens, a key brain area involved in the regulation of reward and motivation.
the effects of chronic alcohol exposure on neuronal excitability, glutamatergicsynaptic transmission and synaptic receptor function in the NAc of rats.
the molecular mechanisms that contribute to the development and persistence of the neuroadaptation in the NAcc that underlie alcohol dependence.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

CIE rats display a hyperpolarization-activated current (Ih) with a larger amplitude, a larger Cs+-sensitive K+ current (IK,IR) with a larger conductance, a larger A-type K+- current (IA, fast A-type) with a larger peak current and a larger conductance and an enhanced AMPAR-mediated miniature excitatory postsynaptic current (mEPSC) with a larger current amplitude and a larger conductances.

chronic intermittent ethanol treatment causes long-lasting changes in the intrinsic properties of medium spiny neuron membrane, and in the properties of glutamatergicsynapses, in the rat nucleus accumbens core.

chronic intermittent ethanol treatment causes long-lasting alterations of excitability and AMPAR function in nucleus accumbens core medium spiny neurons that may contribute to the pathophysiology of alcohol dependence.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

CIE treatment leads to an enhancement in the inward rectification, input resistance, and fAHP, and to a decrease in the AP threshold of NAcc MSNs during protracted withdrawal, and that these alterations in membrane properties are due to increased K+-channel conductance.

the CIE model of alcohol dependence causes significant alterations in the intrinsic electrical and synaptic properties of MSNs in NAcc core, and that these alterations may contribute to the neuroplastic changes in the NAcc that occur during alcohol dependence.

chronic intermittent ethanol treatment followed by prolonged ethanol withdrawal causes long-lasting alterations in membrane properties, K+ currents, and glutamateric synaptic currents of nucleus accumbens medium spiny neurons that are associated with increased neuronal excitability and synaptic efficacy.
The main takeaway from our work is that

chronic intermittent ethanol exposure induces long-lasting changes in the intrinsic properties and glutamategic synaptic transmission in the nucleus accumbens medium spiny neurons that could be important in the neuroadaptations that occur in alcohol dependence.

the CIE treatment protocol used in the current study induces long-lasting changes in the excitability and excitability of MSNs in rat NAcc core, which could play a critical in the neuroadaptive mechanisms underlying alcohol withdrawal and alcohol dependence.
CIE-induced increases in K+-conductances and AMPA-receptor function of NAcc MSNs could contribute to the increased excitability of NAcc MSN observed in alcohol dependence.
